title: When Should Models Change Their Minds? Contextual Belief Management in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2605.30219v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Long-horizon interactions require language models to manage accumulating information: when to update their state, when to preserve their state, and what to ignore. We study this challenge as Contextual Belief Management (CBM): maintaining a predicted belief state aligned with formal evidence while isolating task-irrelevant noise. To make CBM measurable, we introduce BeliefTrack, a closed-world benchmark spanning Rule Discovery and Circuit Diagnosis, where a finite belief space and symbolic verifiers enable exact turn-level evaluation. BeliefTrack diagnoses three failures: Failed Stay, Failed Update, and Failed Isolation. Across multiple LLMs, vanilla models exhibit severe CBM failures, while explicit belief-tracking prompts provide limited gains. translated_title: 模型何时应该改变想法？大型语言模型中的情境信念管理
translated_abstract: 长时程交互要求语言模型管理不断累积的信息：何时更新自身状态、何时保持自身状态，以及应当忽略什么。我们将这一挑战定义为情境信念管理：在隔离与任务无关噪声的同时，维持与正式证据相一致的预测信念状态。为了使CBM可被量化测量，我们引入了BeliefTrack，这是一个涵盖规则发现和电路诊断两类任务的封闭世界基准，其中有限的信念空间和符号验证器能够实现精确的回合级评估。BeliefTrack诊断出三种失败模式：保持失败、更新失败和隔离失败。在多个大语言模型上的实验表明，原始模型表现出严重的CBM失败，而显式的信念跟踪提示仅能带来有限的提升。相比之下，采用信念状态奖励的强化学习平均将失败率降低了70.9%。进一步的探测揭示了这些失败背后的潜在信念状态动态以及表征层面的原因。
tldr: 该论文提出情境信念管理（CBM）新任务及BeliefTrack封闭世界基准，用以精确评估大语言模型在长时程交互中维护、更新和隔离信念状态的能力，并通过信念状态奖励的强化学习将三类失败率平均降低70.9%。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Contextual Belief Management (CBM) and the BeliefTrack closed-world benchmark to precisely evaluate LLMs' ability to maintain, update, and isolate belief states in long-horizon interactions, showing that reinforcement learning with belief-state rewards reduces failure rates by 70.9% on average.
